chat.q: How do I fix spindle overheating?

response.answer:
**SOP-CNC-01 Spindle Overheating Response** (from M1_cnc_milling_manual.pdf, similarity 0.63)
Trigger: spindle temperature above 90 deg C or thermal alarm on the controller.
1. Feed-hold the program and let the spindle run unloaded at 20 percent speed for 5 minutes to cool evenly; do not stop it abruptly.
2. Check coolant flow at the nozzle; flow below 8 L/min points to the coolant pump (see SOP-CNC-03).
3. Inspect the spindle chiller set point (target 22 deg C) and clean the chiller air filter.
4. Verify spindle bearing lubrication: the oil-air unit must show one pulse every 8 minutes.
5. Run the spindle warm-up cycle (O9001) before resuming production.
6. If the temperature exceeds 90 deg C again within 2 hours, raise a ticket and inspect bearing preload.

**SOP-LTH-02 Lathe Spindle Thermal Management** (from M5_cnc_lathe_manual.pdf, similarity 0.57)
1. Run the warm-up program for 15 minutes at the start of each shift.
2. Limit continuous running at maximum speed to 4 hours, then allow a 10 minute idle.
3. Check the spindle oil cooler and coolant concentration if temperature exceeds 85 deg C.

**SOP-HYD-01 Hydraulic Seal Replacement** (from M3_hydraulic_press_manual.pdf, similarity 0.65)
Trigger: oil leakage at the ram, or pressure drop below 170 bar under load.
1. Lower the ram onto safety blocks and apply lockout/tagout (SOP-SAF-01).
2. Release stored hydraulic pressure through the accumulator dump valve; confirm 0 bar on the gauge.
3. Remove the gland nut and extract the worn seal set with a non-metallic pick.

5. Install the new seal kit lubricated with clean hydraulic oil ISO VG

6. Torque the gland nut to 180 Nm, bleed air from the cylinder and test at 210 bar for 10 minutes.
7. Repeated seal failure within 90 days indicates contaminated oil: send an oil sample for analysis.

props.title: SOP-SAF-02 Personal Protective Equipment
props.text: Safety shoes, safety glasses and hearing protection are mandatory on the line. Use cut-resistant gloves when handling tools or chips, and a welding helmet near the welding cell.

props.title: SOP-SAF-03 Emergency Stop and Restart
props.text: 1. Press the nearest emergency stop on any hazard. 2. Report the event to the shift supervisor. 3. Restart only after the cause is cleared and the supervisor resets the safety circuit.

props.title: SOP-CNC-01 Spindle Overheating Response
props.text: Trigger: spindle temperature above 90 deg C or thermal alarm on the controller. 1. Feed-hold the program and let the spindle run unloaded at 20 percent speed for 5 minutes to cool evenly; do not stop it abruptly. 2. Check coolant flow at the nozzle; flow below 8 L/min points to the coolant pump (see SOP-CNC-03). 3. Inspect the spindle chiller set point (target 22 deg C) and clean the chiller air filter. 4. Verify spindle bearing lubrication: the oil-air unit must show one pulse every 8 minutes. 5. Run the spindle warm-up cycle (O9001) before resuming production. 6. If the temperature exceeds 90 deg C again within 2 hours, raise a ticket and inspect bearing preload.

props.title: SOP-CNC-02 Spindle Vibration Diagnosis
props.text: Trigger: vibration above 7.1 mm/s RMS or poor surface finish. 1. Check tool holder runout with a dial indicator; it must be below 5 microns. 2. Clean the spindle taper and the tool holder flange with a lint-free cloth. 3. Balance the tool assembly if spindle speed is above 8000 rpm. 4. Run the vibration spectrum test; a peak at bearing frequency means the bearings need replacement by a CNC technician.

props.title: SOP-CNC-03 Coolant Pump Priming Procedure
props.text: Trigger: low coolant flow alarm or pump not priming at shift start. 1. Apply lockout/tagout to the coolant system (see SOP-SAF-01). 2. Check the coolant tank level; top up with 6 percent emulsion if below the MIN mark. 3. Open the bleed screw on the pump housing until coolant flows without air bubbles, then close it. 4. Clean the suction strainer of chips and sludge. 5. Remove the lockout, run the pump for 2 minutes and confirm flow above 8 L/min.

props.title: SOP-CNC-04 Servo Motor Fault Reset
props.text: Trigger: servo alarm or axis overload on the CNC controller. 1. Record the alarm code and the axis. 2. Check the axis for mechanical obstruction and the ball screw for chips. 3. Inspect the servo motor cable connector for looseness or coolant ingress. 4. Power-cycle the drive and reset the alarm; if it repeats within one shift, replace the encoder cable.

props.title: SOP-ROB-01 Servo Motor Overcurrent Fault
props.text: Trigger: overcurrent or overload alarm on a robot axis. 1. Put the robot in T1 (manual reduced speed) mode and jog the faulted axis slowly. 2. Check for collisions, cable snags or a payload heavier than the configured value. 3. Measure motor winding insulation with a megger; it must be above 100 megaohm. 4. Inspect the axis gearbox for backlash. 5. If the fault repeats, replace the servo motor and run the payload identification routine.

props.title: SOP-ROB-02 Encoder Error and Re-homing
props.text: Trigger: encoder error or robot lost home position. 1. Check the encoder battery voltage on the controller; replace if below 3.0 V. 2. Jog each axis to its witness mark. 3. Run the mastering (re-homing) routine from the teach pendant and verify with the TCP check point.

props.title: SOP-ROB-03 Gripper Vacuum Loss
props.text: 1. Check the vacuum generator supply air pressure, required 6 bar. 2. Inspect suction cups for tears and replace worn cups. 3. Clean the vacuum filter and test that vacuum reaches minus 0.6 bar within 0.3 seconds.

props.title: SOP-ROB-04 Welding Torch Nozzle Cleaning
props.text: 1. Move the torch to the cleaning station. 2. Run the reamer cycle and spray anti-spatter fluid. 3. Replace the contact tip if the bore is worn oval, typically every 8 hours of arc time.

props.title: SOP-ROB-05 Wire Feeder Slip Correction
props.text: 1. Check drive roll groove size matches the wire diameter. 2. Set drive roll tension so the wire stops when pinched at the gun. 3. Blow out the liner with dry air and replace it if kinked.

props.title: SOP-HYD-01 Hydraulic Seal Replacement
props.text: Trigger: oil leakage at the ram, or pressure drop below 170 bar under load. 1. Lower the ram onto safety blocks and apply lockout/tagout (SOP-SAF-01). 2. Release stored hydraulic pressure through the accumulator dump valve; confirm 0 bar on the gauge. 3. Remove the gland nut and extract the worn seal set with a non-metallic pick. 4. Inspect the cylinder rod for scoring; polish minor marks, replace the rod if scoring is deeper than 0.1 mm. 5. Install the new seal kit lubricated with clean hydraulic oil ISO VG 46. 6. Torque the gland nut to 180 Nm, bleed air from the cylinder and test at 210 bar for 10 minutes. 7. Repeated seal failure within 90 days indicates contaminated oil: send an oil sample for analysis.

props.title: SOP-HYD-02 Hydraulic Pump Cavitation
props.text: Trigger: whining noise from the pump or foaming oil. 1. Check the reservoir oil level and top up to the sight-glass mark. 2. Inspect the suction line and clamps for air leaks. 3. Replace the suction filter if the differential pressure indicator is red. 4. Verify oil temperature is between 40 and 55 deg C; cold oil causes cavitation at start-up.

props.title: SOP-HYD-03 Pressure Valve Calibration
props.text: 1. Install a calibrated test gauge on port P1. 2. Adjust the relief valve until the system relieves at 210 bar plus or minus 2 bar. 3. Lock the adjustment screw and record the setting in the maintenance log.

props.title: SOP-CNV-01 Drive Belt Alignment and Tensioning
props.text: Trigger: belt fraying, drifting or slipping. 1. Apply lockout/tagout to the conveyor drive (SOP-SAF-01). 2. Check pulley alignment with a straight edge; adjust the take-up screws equally on both sides. 3. Set belt tension so mid-span deflection is 1 percent of the span length. 4. Run empty for 10 minutes and confirm the belt tracks centrally.

props.title: SOP-CNV-02 Drive Belt Replacement
props.text: 1. Lockout the drive and release tension at the take-up. 2. Remove the old belt and inspect pulleys and rollers for wear or seized bearings. 3. Fit the new belt, re-tension per SOP-CNV-01 and record the change date.

props.title: SOP-LTH-01 Chuck Jaw Clamping Check
props.text: 1. Clean the jaws and the chuck body serrations. 2. Grease the chuck through the nipples with chuck paste, 2 strokes each. 3. Measure clamping force with a gauge; it must be within 10 percent of the rated value. 4. Bore soft jaws again if runout exceeds 0.02 mm.

props.title: SOP-LTH-02 Lathe Spindle Thermal Management
props.text: 1. Run the warm-up program for 15 minutes at the start of each shift. 2. Limit continuous running at maximum speed to 4 hours, then allow a 10 minute idle. 3. Check the spindle oil cooler and coolant concentration if temperature exceeds 85 deg C.

PUB-MACHINE-GUARDING-1.text: Types of guarding. One or more methods of machine guarding shall be provided to protect the operator and other employees in the machine area from hazards such as those created by point of operation, ingoing nip points, rotating parts, flying chips and sparks. Examples of guarding methods are - barrier guards, two-hand tripping devices, electronic safety devices, etc. General requirements for machine guards. Guards shall be affixed to the machine where possible and secured elsewhere if for any reason attachment to the machine is not possible. The guard shall be such that it does not offer an accident hazard in itself. The point of operation of machines whose operation exposes an employee to injury, shall be guarded. The guarding device shall be in conformity with any appropriate standards therefor, or, in the absence of applicable specific standards, shall be so designed and constructed as to prevent the operator from having any part of his body in the danger zone during the operating cycle. SOP-SAF-03.label: SOP
SOP-SAF-03.title: SOP-SAF-03 Emergency Stop and Restart
SOP-SAF-03.text: 1. Press the nearest emergency stop on any hazard. 2. Report the event to the shift supervisor. 3. Restart only after the cause is cleared and the supervisor resets the safety circuit.

SOP-CNC-01.label: SOP
SOP-CNC-01.title: SOP-CNC-01 Spindle Overheating Response
SOP-CNC-01.text: Trigger: spindle temperature above 90 deg C or thermal alarm on the controller. 1. Feed-hold the program and let the spindle run unloaded at 20 percent speed for 5 minutes to cool evenly; do not stop it abruptly. 2. Check coolant flow at the nozzle; flow below 8 L/min points to the coolant pump (see SOP-CNC-03). 3. Inspect the spindle chiller set point (target 22 deg C) and clean the chiller air filter. 4. Verify spindle bearing lubrication: the oil-air unit must show one pulse every 8 minutes. 5. Run the spindle warm-up cycle (O9001) before resuming production. 6. If the temperature exceeds 90 deg C again within 2 hours, raise a ticket and inspect bearing preload.

SOP-CNC-02.label: SOP
SOP-CNC-02.title: SOP-CNC-02 Spindle Vibration Diagnosis
SOP-CNC-02.text: Trigger: vibration above 7.1 mm/s RMS or poor surface finish. 1. Check tool holder runout with a dial indicator; it must be below 5 microns. 2. Clean the spindle taper and the tool holder flange with a lint-free cloth. 3. Balance the tool assembly if spindle speed is above 8000 rpm. 4. Run the vibration spectrum test; a peak at bearing frequency means the bearings need replacement by a CNC technician.

SOP-CNC-03.label: SOP
SOP-CNC-03.title: SOP-CNC-03 Coolant Pump Priming Procedure
SOP-CNC-03.text: Trigger: low coolant flow alarm or pump not priming at shift start. 1. Apply lockout/tagout to the coolant system (see SOP-SAF-01). 2. Check the coolant tank level; top up with 6 percent emulsion if below the MIN mark. 3. Open the bleed screw on the pump housing until coolant flows without air bubbles, then close it. 4. Clean the suction strainer of chips and sludge. 5. Remove the lockout, run the pump for 2 minutes and confirm flow above 8 L/min.

SOP-CNC-04.label: SOP
SOP-CNC-04.title: SOP-CNC-04 Servo Motor Fault Reset
SOP-CNC-04.text: Trigger: servo alarm or axis overload on the CNC controller. 1. Record the alarm code and the axis. 2. Check the axis for mechanical obstruction and the ball screw for chips. 3. Inspect the servo motor cable connector for looseness or coolant ingress. 4. Power-cycle the drive and reset the alarm; if it repeats within one shift, replace the encoder cable.

SOP-ROB-01.label: SOP
SOP-ROB-01.title: SOP-ROB-01 Servo Motor Overcurrent Fault
SOP-ROB-01.text: Trigger: overcurrent or overload alarm on a robot axis. 1. Put the robot in T1 (manual reduced speed) mode and jog the faulted axis slowly. 2. Check for collisions, cable snags or a payload heavier than the configured value. 3. Measure motor winding insulation with a megger; it must be above 100 megaohm. 4. Inspect the axis gearbox for backlash. 5. If the fault repeats, replace the servo motor and run the payload identification routine.

SOP-ROB-02.label: SOP
SOP-ROB-02.title: SOP-ROB-02 Encoder Error and Re-homing
SOP-ROB-02.text: Trigger: encoder error or robot lost home position. 1. Check the encoder battery voltage on the controller; replace if below 3.0 V. 2. Jog each axis to its witness mark. 3. Run the mastering (re-homing) routine from the teach pendant and verify with the TCP check point.

SOP-ROB-03.label: SOP
SOP-ROB-03.title: SOP-ROB-03 Gripper Vacuum Loss
SOP-ROB-03.text: 1. Check the vacuum generator supply air pressure, required 6 bar. 2. Inspect suction cups for tears and replace worn cups. 3. Clean the vacuum filter and test that vacuum reaches minus 0.6 bar within 0.3 seconds.

SOP-ROB-04.label: SOP
SOP-ROB-04.title: SOP-ROB-04 Welding Torch Nozzle Cleaning
SOP-ROB-04.text: 1. Move the torch to the cleaning station. 2. Run the reamer cycle and spray anti-spatter fluid. 3. Replace the contact tip if the bore is worn oval, typically every 8 hours of arc time.

SOP-ROB-05.label: SOP
SOP-ROB-05.title: SOP-ROB-05 Wire Feeder Slip Correction
SOP-ROB-05.text: 1. Check drive roll groove size matches the wire diameter. 2. Set drive roll tension so the wire stops when pinched at the gun. 3. Blow out the liner with dry air and replace it if kinked.

SOP-HYD-01.label: SOP
SOP-HYD-01.title: SOP-HYD-01 Hydraulic Seal Replacement
SOP-HYD-01.text: Trigger: oil leakage at the ram, or pressure drop below 170 bar under load. 1. Lower the ram onto safety blocks and apply lockout/tagout (SOP-SAF-01). 2. Release stored hydraulic pressure through the accumulator dump valve; confirm 0 bar on the gauge. 3. Remove the gland nut and extract the worn seal set with a non-metallic pick. 4. Inspect the cylinder rod for scoring; polish minor marks, replace the rod if scoring is deeper than 0.1 mm. 5. Install the new seal kit lubricated with clean hydraulic oil ISO VG 46. 6. Torque the gland nut to 180 Nm, bleed air from the cylinder and test at 210 bar for 10 minutes. 7. Repeated seal failure within 90 days indicates contaminated oil: send an oil sample for analysis.

SOP-HYD-02.label: SOP
SOP-HYD-02.title: SOP-HYD-02 Hydraulic Pump Cavitation
SOP-HYD-02.text: Trigger: whining noise from the pump or foaming oil. 1. Check the reservoir oil level and top up to the sight-glass mark. 2. Inspect the suction line and clamps for air leaks. 3. Replace the suction filter if the differential pressure indicator is red. 4. Verify oil temperature is between 40 and 55 deg C; cold oil causes cavitation at start-up.

SOP-HYD-03.label: SOP
SOP-HYD-03.title: SOP-HYD-03 Pressure Valve Calibration
SOP-HYD-03.text: 1. Install a calibrated test gauge on port P1. 2. Adjust the relief valve until the system relieves at 210 bar plus or minus 2 bar. 3. Lock the adjustment screw and record the setting in the maintenance log.

SOP-CNV-01.label: SOP
SOP-CNV-01.title: SOP-CNV-01 Drive Belt Alignment and Tensioning
SOP-CNV-01.text: Trigger: belt fraying, drifting or slipping. 1. Apply lockout/tagout to the conveyor drive (SOP-SAF-01). 2. Check pulley alignment with a straight edge; adjust the take-up screws equally on both sides. 3. Set belt tension so mid-span deflection is 1 percent of the span length. 4. Run empty for 10 minutes and confirm the belt tracks centrally.

SOP-CNV-02.label: SOP
SOP-CNV-02.title: SOP-CNV-02 Drive Belt Replacement
SOP-CNV-02.text: 1. Lockout the drive and release tension at the take-up. 2. Remove the old belt and inspect pulleys and rollers for wear or seized bearings. 3. Fit the new belt, re-tension per SOP-CNV-01 and record the change date.

SOP-LTH-01.label: SOP
SOP-LTH-01.title: SOP-LTH-01 Chuck Jaw Clamping Check
SOP-LTH-01.text: 1. Clean the jaws and the chuck body serrations. 2. Grease the chuck through the nipples with chuck paste, 2 strokes each. 3. Measure clamping force with a gauge; it must be within 10 percent of the rated value. 4. Bore soft jaws again if runout exceeds 0.02 mm.

SOP-LTH-02.label: SOP
SOP-LTH-02.title: SOP-LTH-02 Lathe Spindle Thermal Management
SOP-LTH-02.text: 1. Run the warm-up program for 15 minutes at the start of each shift. 2. Limit continuous running at maximum speed to 4 hours, then allow a 10 minute idle. 3. Check the spindle oil cooler and coolant concentration if temperature exceeds 85 deg C.
